PullRequest.Title: sessions: stop the activity bar from rechecking pull request openers on every state update
PullRequest.Body:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

The Agents window logged thousands of `Canceled: Canceled` errors a minute, worst right after a window reload, all from the activity bar's pull request opener check. The editor window logs none.

## Cause

- `SessionChatInputToolbar` decides which pull request buttons the activity bar shows by asking the registered external URI openers whether they can open each pull request link. The check is a `derived` keyed on `activityBarOpenerRefs`, which used `structuralEquals`.
- `structuralEquals` compares only plain objects and arrays by value; it treats two `URI` instances of the same link as different. Session state updates recreate the `URI`s of unchanged links, so every update looked like a change, restarted the check and cancelled the previous `canOpen` calls to the extension host.
- `ExternalUriOpenerService.getValidOpeners` logged each cancelled `canOpen` as an error.

## Changes

- Compare the opener refs by id and link value (`isEqual`), so only real link changes restart the check.
- Don't log cancellation errors from `canOpen`; other failures are still logged.

## Testing

- New test: recreating the same links 10 times caused 10 opener lookups before the fix and 0 after.
- New test: a cancelled opener is not logged, a failing one still is.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionChatInputToolbar.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/externalUriOpener/test/common/externalUriOpenerService.test.ts`: passed (97 tests).
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed. `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: passed.
- Live, Code - OSS dev builds with an isolated copy of a real profile (Settings Sync off), Agents window restoring a session with a pull request. Opener `canOpen` calls counted with a non-pausing breakpoint, 90 s after a window reload: **219 before the fix, 3 after**; 0 while idle after the fix. `Canceled` errors in the log: 561 before, 0 after.

## Regression

Likely regression: the opener check came with #343557, and #343787 added the `structuralEquals` comparison to avoid repeated lookups. Its test only changed titles on the same `URI` instances, so recreated `URI`s were never covered.

## Review

Independent review on a different model: approved, no actionable findings.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Equivalent pull-request URIs reconstructed on session state updates failed structural equality, repeatedly invalidating the activity-bar opener derivation. Each invalidation spawned a concurrent opener lookup for every PR and every contributed opener, cancelling in-flight requests and potentially logging those cancellation failures.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: High-frequency session updates caused repeated and cancelled extension-host canOpen IPC and associated cancellation-log churn, scaling with update frequency, pull-request references, and registered openers.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new equality function compares each stable artifact id and URI value with resources.isEqual, so equivalent reconstructed links no longer invalidate activityBarOpeners. Real id/link changes plus extension/configuration signals still trigger revalidation, preserving intended refresh semantics while removing repeated opener discovery, cancellation, and extension-host IPC.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 629 used structuralEquals for arrays containing URI instances. structuralEquals only recursively compares arrays and plain objects, so a state refresh that recreates an equivalent URI makes activityBarOpenerRefs look changed. That invalidates activityBarOpeners, cancels its prior token, and reruns Promise.all(refs.map(...externalUriOpenerService.getOpener...)). getOpener calls getValidOpeners, which invokes every registered opener's canOpen concurrently; MainThreadUriOpeners implements canOpen with proxy.$canOpenUri, an extension-host IPC. The added test recreates identical links ten times and now observes zero additional lookups.

Scenarios.Scenario: Session/activity-bar refresh recreates unchanged pull-request URI objects
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The observable equality check runs synchronously when pull-request references update. When values are unchanged, the new comparator stops invalidation before asynchronous opener discovery; activity-bar support therefore makes progress without waiting for any new lookup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke contributed external URI opener canOpen logic in the extension host via proxy.$canOpenUri.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the fix, up to R x O calls per equivalent state refresh for R pull-request references and O matching registered openers; after the fix, zero calls for equivalent reconstructed links.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base comparator treated reconstructed URI instances as unequal and re-entered opener discovery on every such refresh; the diff removes those repeated calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The calls asynchronously determine which PR activity-bar actions are supported; repeated invalidations replace and cancel pending checks. The new equality check avoids this boundary entirely on unchanged refreshes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost previously scaled with session-state update frequency multiplied by the number of effective pull-request references and matching contributed openers. The added test models ten equivalent updates; production cardinality is bounded by the session's displayed PR references but update frequency can be high.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: After the change, equivalent refreshes schedule no opener work. Before the change, each refresh started all PR lookups concurrently, and each lookup checked all contributed openers concurrently; there is no shared limiter, while replacement invalidations cancel the prior token.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Initial/cold evaluation still resolves all refs. supportedOpenerUris preserves positive support only for interim display and does not skip authoritative revalidation. The new value comparator acts as coalescing for warm equivalent updates; real URL/id, extension, or configuration changes still invalidate. Negative results are not cached across genuine invalidations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: structuralEquals rejects distinct URI instances, the changed derivation feeds the Promise.all lookup fan-out, and the added test verifies zero lookups for ten reconstructed equivalent links.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact PR/openers counts and extension response times vary, but the removed invalidation and R x O IPC mechanism are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: This is a performance improvement, not a regression. The new O(R) value comparison prevents a much more expensive repeated asynchronous boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial activity-bar load or a genuine PR link/id, extension, or opener-configuration change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The comparator or openerChanges signal invalidates activityBarOpeners; support checks run asynchronously before the authoritative supported set is updated. Previously supported URIs may remain visible while revalidation is pending.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call each contributed opener's canOpenExternalUri implementation in the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: R x O calls for R distinct displayed PR refs and O registered openers applicable to HTTP(S), both before and after the diff when authoritative revalidation is required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same nested Promise.all fan-out occurred for initial and genuine invalidations; the diff does not increase its cardinality or concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The checks are asynchronous and determine final action availability; retained previous support can keep existing actions usable while checks are pending.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of displayed PR references and registered matching openers controls fan-out. The new equality comparison is linear in PR references, comparable to the prior array structural comparison.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All effective PR references are checked with Promise.all, and each getValidOpeners checks all effective openers with another Promise.all. There is no global limiter, unchanged from the base behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold initialization performs checks. Warm equivalent updates are now coalesced; genuine changes intentionally bypass that coalescing. supportedOpenerUris carries positive prior state for display but is not an authoritative lookup cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed and surrounding code explicitly show equality invalidation, nested Promise.all calls, and extension-host proxy dispatch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The typical number of PR references and openers is not established, but no changed mechanism increases work on this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Required revalidations retain prior behavior, while equivalent updates become cheaper.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cancellation or failure while validating external URI openers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: getValidOpeners waits for all concurrent canOpen promises before selecting an opener. The changed catch only alters cancellation logging; it does not add waits or boundary calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run canOpen checks in registered providers, including extension-host proxy calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per effective opener for each getOpener request, unchanged by the logging guard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same canOpen calls ran and cancellation rejections were returned as unsupported entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Promise settlement remains on opener selection's critical path; the new guard does not change call scheduling or completion semantics.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit an error through ILogService for a rejected canOpen call, potentially writing the workbench log.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, one log emission per rejected opener including expected cancellations; after the diff, cancellation errors emit none while non-cancellation failures still emit one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cancellation and failure rejections were both logged; the diff suppresses only cancellation logging.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Logging occurs in the rejection catch before Promise.all settles; the diff removes that work for cancellation and does not add critical-path I/O.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Boundary and former log work scale with getOpener frequency and matching opener count; cancellation churn additionally scales with replacement invalidations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All openers are checked concurrently with Promise.all, unchanged. Cancellation propagates through each opener token; rejected entries are filtered from the result.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache is added or removed. The toolbar comparator now prevents the main source of repeated replacement cancellations for equivalent links; normal opener failures remain uncached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the catch guard and test directly distinguish CancellationError from ordinary failure, while all upstream calls remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual logging backend flush behavior and cancellation frequency outside the toolbar are not established, but the changed path only removes work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change reduces cancellation-log CPU/allocation/I/O and preserves logging for real failures.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and all diff pages. Traced observable invalidation, nested opener discovery, extension-host canOpen IPC, cancellation, logging, caching, and concurrency. The PR fixes repeated R x O opener checks on equivalent state updates and introduces no actionable performance regression.
